target_columns.name: policy_id
target_columns.transformation: BY-group merge key between policies_sorted and claims_agg_sorted, both pre-sorted by policy_id.

target_columns.name: product_line
target_columns.transformation: Passed through unchanged from policies; also becomes the primary key of the final output sort order.

target_columns.name: sum_insured
target_columns.transformation: Passed through unchanged from policies; used as the denominator for severity_ratio.

target_columns.name: <other policy attributes>
target_columns.transformation: All remaining policy columns are carried through unchanged from policies_sorted via the DATA step merge.

target_columns.name: claim_count
target_columns.transformation: COUNT(*) of claims grouped by policy_id (PROC SQL); zero-filled when the policy has no matching claims record.

target_columns.name: total_claim_amount
target_columns.transformation: SUM(claim_amount) grouped by policy_id; zero-filled when the policy has no matching claims record.

target_columns.name: max_claim_amount
target_columns.transformation: MAX(claim_amount) grouped by policy_id; zero-filled when the policy has no matching claims record.

target_columns.name: severity_ratio
target_columns.transformation: max_claim_amount / sum_insured when sum_insured > 0, else hardcoded to 0 to avoid division by zero/negative.

target_columns.name: severity_flag
target_columns.transformation: IF-THEN/ELSE recode: 'HIGH' if severity_ratio >= 0.5, 'MEDIUM' if >= 0.25, else 'LOW'.

target_columns.name: high_severity_count
target_columns.transformation: RETAIN counter incremented by 1 each time severity_flag = 'HIGH', accumulated in policy_id merge-traversal order; not explicitly dropped, so it leaks into the output as a running cumulative count rather than a per-row or per-group total.

quirks: Both inputs must be pre-sorted by policy_id before the DATA step MERGE/BY -- PySpark has no implicit sort-merge BY-group semantics, so this ordering must be made explicit (e.g. window functions) or the merge logic re-derived via explicit joins.

The MERGE with 'if in_pol;' implements a left-outer join keyed on policy_id: every policy row is kept (claims zero-filled if absent), while any claim rows whose policy_id has no matching policy record are silently dropped. This is not a full outer or inner join and must be preserved exactly.

high_severity_count is a RETAIN variable that is never reset and never dropped (only in_pol/in_claims are dropped), so it survives into the final output table as an order-dependent running tally of HIGH-severity rows seen so far during the policy_id-sorted merge pass -- it is NOT a per-row or per-policy aggregate.

The final output is re-sorted by product_line, policy_id, which is a different order than the policy_id-only order the RETAIN counter was computed in -- so in the output, high_severity_count values appear out of their accumulation sequence and look inconsistent/non-monotonic per row unless the original merge order is reconstructed.
severity_ratio divide-by-zero guard treats sum_insured <= 0 as 0 ratio (silently, no null/error raised) -- must be replicated rather than letting Spark produce null/NaN or raise on division by zero.

The 'if in_claims then do; claim_count = claim_count; ... end;' block is a no-op reassignment (quirk of legacy style, not an actual transformation) -- only the else branch (zero-fill) has real effect.

This reference re-implementation is a legacy SQL/DATA-step pipeline, not the original SAS engine output -- any reconciliation against it must be reported as validation against a re-implemented baseline, not the true legacy system, per repo convention.
